result.title: PaperFormalizer: Author-in-the-Loop Autoformalization of Research Papers in Lean
result.summary: Even a carefully proofread paper can leave small gaps in its proofs or its stated assumptions. We introduce PaperFormalizer, a Lean-based agentic pipeline that helps authors find and close such gaps in their own papers and turn each paper into a Lean-verified version. Starting from the LaTeX source, PaperFormalizer transcribes the paper into a dependency graph of statements, audits each statement in natural language for faithfulness, ambiguity and correctness, and then formalizes and proves the statements in Lean against Mathlib, optional domain libraries and the author's personal toolkit. Only the author knows what a statement is meant to say and how a formalization gap in a result is best fixed. The pipeline therefore stops and asks the author whenever a statement admits more than one reading, presents every repair, in natural language and TeX symbols, as a proposal that the author can accept, decline or redirect, and leaves to the author every decision that could potentially change what the paper claims. The output is an annotated and revised version of the paper, a report of the changes, and Lean code in which each declaration is linked to the statement it formalizes. The author's toolkit grows as more papers are formalized, and authors can share their verified papers so that researchers who build on them can reuse their Lean code. By making verified papers practical to produce, PaperFormalizer aims to make research that rests on mathematical proofs more robust. PaperFormalizer runs inside a coding agent (Claude Code or Codex) and is available at https://github.com/Jiyuan-Tan/PaperFormalizer. Papers with Lean code shared by users are available at https://paperformalizer.org.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 PaperFormalizer：在编码智能体中把论文 LaTeX 源码转成语句依赖图，逐条做自然语言审计，再在 Lean/Mathlib 中形式化并证明；遇歧义或需修复时暂停并交由作者接受、拒绝或改向，最终产出修订论文、变更报告及与语句对应的 Lean 代码。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「分解—审计—形式化验证—人审修订」流程可供核查如何为 latent 推理的中间结论提供可验证监督与停止/改向信号，但论文本身不涉及视觉或多模态推理，迁移需较多改造。
